bug_info.bug_desc: The advance-operation KMAC payloads were constructed with the wrong seed/data blocks. For the Initialized-to-CreatorRootKey advance, `adv_matrix[Creator]` included both `revision_seed` and `creator_seed` as 256-bit data blocks, even though the spec requires this transition to use only one hardware-revision-secret diversification block and does not include the flash creator seed in the data payload. For the CreatorRootKey-to-OwnerIntermediateKey advance, `adv_matrix[OwnerInt]` used `owner_seed`, but the spec requires the creator seed. For the OwnerIntermediateKey-to-OwnerKey advance, `adv_matrix[Owner]` contained only `sw_binding` and omitted the required `owner_seed` block. The `keymgr_pkg::AdvDataWidth` parameter was also sized for three key-width blocks, which matches the old oversized/misaligned Creator payload but not the corrected two-key-block payload layout. As a result, the KMAC messages, and therefore the derived internal keys, were computed from the wrong advance diversification inputs and the specified key-derivation domain separation was violated.
bug_info.fix_hint: Reorganize the advance payload concatenations so each advance transition uses the state-appropriate single key-width seed block: omit `creator_seed` from `adv_matrix[Creator]` and keep `revision_seed` as the one derivation block; use `creator_seed` in `adv_matrix[OwnerInt]` instead of `owner_seed`; and add `owner_seed` to `adv_matrix[Owner]` alongside `sw_binding`. Update `keymgr_pkg::AdvDataWidth` to `SwBindingWidth + 2*KeyWidth + DevIdWidth + HealthStateWidth` so the width matches the new maximum payload size.
